body:
Missing-update handling is a caller-selected policy. The follow-up comments on #517 require retaining the unchecked raw route; inserting mandatory backend checks would contradict the architecture decision from PR #527.

Research confirms that the existing outer `LinksInnerReferenceExistenceValidator<T>`, per-call `EnsureLinkExists`, and an explicit existence branch already provide the requested choices. This PR adds documentation, executable recipes and regression coverage without changing runtime behavior.

Fixes #517.

### Changes

- Document update preconditions, validator scope and ordering, address versus endpoint checks, no-op policies, overload results, callbacks, concurrency and reused addresses. Add API remarks and links from both READMEs and documentation navigation.
- Preserve the unchecked raw and automatic-resolution routes. Explain why the validator belongs outside resolvers and why it is broader than checking only the updated address.
- Add `examples/Update` for both backends and plain/automatic stacks, and run it in Linux/Windows C# CI. Include the example and investigation in generated documentation.
- Add a C# patch changeset for the existing automatic release workflow.

### Reproduction and verification

Both original scenarios are exercised through an explicitly selected checked boundary: update never-created address 10 after creating points, or delete the middle of three points and attempt to update that address. Requests throw before resolver work; contents, counts, source/target queries and allocator reuse remain unchanged. Following `CreateAndUpdate` remains allocated and searchable. Invalid raw writes are never used as in-process regression probes.

`UpdateContractTests` adds 105 cases. The 96-case missing-update matrix runs byte/ushort/uint/ulong across both backends, plain/automatic stacks, throwing/skipping policies, missing/deleted/empty scenarios and existing/absent pairs. Each case checks the address adapter, handler overload and primitive null-handler form. Other tests cover valid unchecked updates, valid checked results/callbacks, validator ordering and service-constant scope.

The first 100 cases pass against the existing implementation before library/documentation changes, supporting the decision that runtime changes are unnecessary. The bounded `experiments/verify_update_contract_guards.py` temporarily adds mandatory raw checks and removes the validator only in a terminal-spy test: exactly three tests fail. Sources are restored, and the full suite passes afterward. The probe requires a fresh TRX report; a failed command cannot reuse a previous result.

Local validation:

- Full Release C# suite: **298 passed, no skips**; all three executable examples, formatting, packaging and isolated package consumer pass.
- Pipeline regressions: **65 passed**; repository configuration, workflow lint, Markdown lint, Bandit, the experiment docstring check, release-fragment validation and full-history credential scanning pass.
- DocFX and Doxygen: no warnings/errors; **549 HTML pages**, local links and Unicode source PDF validated.
- Native suite: **46 passed**; benchmark smoke, formatting, Clang-Tidy and Cppcheck pass with sequential builds.

All applicable hosted checks pass on final commit `243bdd4991506b2e7e867d17d71f43f5ffa4c432`: [CI run 40871156288](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/actions/runs/40871156288) covers Linux/Windows C#, GCC/Clang, sanitizers, documentation, dependency/security auditing and CodeQL for C#, C++ and Actions. Codacy also passes. Current `main` is merged.

The [research inventory](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/issue-517-8bdec171952f/docs/update-investigation.md) maps the issue and later comments to evidence. No required sub-issues were listed; the separate Rust/index/allocation findings from PR #527 are not prerequisites of this C# update investigation.
